title: Rarity and how it is chosen
summary: Rarity in TCG Card Shop Simulator is a fixed set of levels rather than a number you type: the game defines a rarity setting and gives choosing a rarity its own screen.
body: Rarity is a defined set of levels in the game, which is why a card is described by a level rather than by a free value.
Choosing a rarity is a deliberate action with its own screen, so setting a card's rarity is a step in handling it rather than an automatic side effect.
Because rarity is part of how a card is presented, it travels with the card and is separate from what the card is worth to you.
What this entry does not tell you: how many rarity levels there are, the odds of pulling each one, or how rarity changes a card's price. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Rarity is a fixed set of levels in the game.
Choosing a rarity happens in its own screen.
The game ships a card icon of its own for each rarity it names.
facts.evidence: asset names: CardIcon_Common, CardIcon_Rare, CardIcon_Epic, CardIcon_Legend

facts.claim: The build also ships the materials for a rare pack, including one for a named line of packs.
Foil is something the interface talks about itself: the build names foil text, no-foil text, a foil mask for a card and a set of foil sheets.
facts.evidence: asset names: FoilText, NoFoilText, CardFoilMask, M_CardFoilUI

facts.claim: Foil is drawn in world space as well: the build names blended and world-space foil sheets, plus a shine and a glitter pass for the camera.
facts.evidence: asset names: M_CardFoilUITextured_Blended, M_CardFoilUI_World, CameraFoilShine, CameraFoilShine_Glitter

facts.claim: The top rarity has a glow of its own, a glow texture with an alpha version and an interface material, and it has packs named for it as well.
facts.evidence: asset names: T_CardLegendGlow, T_CardLegendGlowAlpha2, M_CardLegendGlowUI, PackLegend, PackDestinyLegendary
